What is an APS?
• Obtain a National Senior Certificate (NSC) or International Secondary Certificate (ISC), issued by Umalusi, which also

indicates that you meet the requirements for a bachelor’s degree.
• An NSC with a minimum of 50% in any four NSC 20-credit subjects.

• APS is calculated using six subjects, excluding Life Orientation. Since Life Orientation isn’t included at NWU, however most
faculties at the NWU recommend a 60% pass in Life Orientation.
• Subject-specific requirements per faculty, which include the language of learning and teaching at 50%.

The Admission Point Score (APS) helps universities assess if you meet the entry requirements for your chosen course. It’s based
on your Grade 11 or 12 results from your six best-performing subjects, excluding Life Orientation. Each subject earns points
depending on your percentage.

The APS is a key factor in determining eligibility for specific programmes. NWU’s APS Calculator allows you to calculate your score
for NSC, International Secondary Certificate (ISC), and SACAI results, and check if you qualify for the programme you wish to
apply to.

The Cambridge International curriculum is the most widely used international examination.

a South African Grade 12.

APS Calculation by Level:
• O/IGCSE Levels: Begin at a score of 5 for the lowest level.

• AS Levels: Equivalent to the South African matric; grades above 90% earn an APS of 8, while grades of 80% and above
earn 7, and so on.
• A Levels: Equivalent to a first-year university level; a grade of A earns the highest score, APS = 10.

Calculate your APS based on six (6) subjects, using the highest level passed in each subject.
Note:
• For qualifications that require Physical Science as a subject, both Physics and Chemistry are mandatory.
• Mathematics is accepted at AS Levels.

Internal and External Bursaries
Studying takes hard work, but also requires funding. To help you finance your academic future, we have compiled a list of bursary
schemes
Internal Bursaries
Academic Merit Bursary Own your academic journey and pay for your studies. The Academic Merit Bursary is available to all fulltime first-, second-, third- and fourth-year students who complete their degree within its relevant duration, e.g., within three years
for a three-year degree. To qualify for this bursary, you must meet specific academic requirements. Part-time students must apply
and qualify for half of the allocation.
Family Discount Families with two or more students registered simultaneously at NWU can apply for this bursary and will receive
a percentage discount on class fees, depending on whether you are the second, third, or fourth family member. One student must
apply annually, and it is not awarded automatically.
Arts and Culture Bursary Students qualify based on their achievements in arts and culture from Grades 8-12. To apply, visit: Arts

and Culture Bursary. The Department of Arts and Culture will assess your application. Senior students qualify based on participation
in cultural activities at university, e.g., NWU choir, symphony orchestra, and others.
Leadership Bursary Were you a head boy, head girl, or a chairman in Grade 12? Thanks to the once-off leadership bursary, you
can get an additional discount on your first year of study.
Support Bursary NWU offers bursaries to prospective students with physical disabilities or students who come from an orphanage
or foster care system. The relevant student must have university admission before applying and need only apply once. Ensure all
necessary documents are attached to the application form: Support Bursary Form.
Sports Bursary The NWU Sport Department only awards bursaries to contracted students. Prospective students with provincial
colours can apply for a sports bursary in the year before they plan to study at NWU. For more information, click here!

A significant number of bursary opportunities are available outside of NWU.

NWU Arts
NWU Arts offers a distinctive combination of academic excellence and hands-on experience. Whether your passion lies in visual
arts, performing arts, or digital media, NWU provides a platform to cultivate your creativity and refine your skills under the mentorship

of accomplished faculty members and industry professionals.
North-West University’s arts community is a dynamic hub of ideas, where collaborative and interdisciplinary projects thrive, allowing
you to work alongside fellow #NWUEagles. This collaborative spirit reflects the real-world creative industries, equipping you for a
future where versatility and adaptability are essential.
NWU’s state-of-the-art facilities, studios, performance spaces, and galleries are designed to inspire and support your artistic journey.

5 easy tips for seamless application process.
1. Have an active email address ready

2. Know your desired study field options’ minimum admission requirements
3. Prepare your supporting documents digitally
4. Create an application profile and complete fields thoroughly
5. Accept your conditional acceptance offer within the limited time frame
Ready to apply? Follow these steps!
• Register: Visit the NWU application system and create your profile by registering with your personal details as shown on your
ID document.
• Confirmation: You’ll receive your username (email address) and temporary password via email. Use these to log in to the
application system.
Create Your Application Profile
• Use your username and password to access the application system. Be sure not to change your email address or phone
number throughout the year, as all important communication will be sent to these contacts.
Log In
• Select up to two study programmes that interest you. For detailed information on qualifications, delivery methods, and
curriculums, visit our yearbooks
• Note: Study options are linked to specific campuses. Ensure you choose the correct campus if your preferred programme is
not listed.
Choose Your Study Options
• Prepare and upload the following documents in a digital format (PDF, JPEG, etc.):
• Certified copy of your ID document.
• Final Grade 11 or 12 results.
• If applicable, a copy of your academic records.
• For International Students:
• Certified copy of your passport.
• Most recent academic records and qualifications.
• Medical examination according to your country’s requirements.
• Apply for an evaluation certificate from the South African Qualifications Authority (SAQA) after completing your high school
career.
Upload Supporting Documents
• Review all your information and read the declaration on the final screen before you submit it.
Submit Your Application
Watch our application video for step-by-step guidance
Please note: An application that has not been submitted cannot be processed by NWU.
